Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Solara Renewables Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad at that time. There will be an opportunity to ask a follow-up question, again by pressing star one. To withdraw your question, please press star two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Solara Renewables' results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Financial Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Marcus Green, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Taylor Brooks, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Solara Renewables delivered exceptional results in the Q3, showcasing our leadership in the renewable energy sector. Our success is attributable to our innovative technologies, strategic partnerships, and unwavering commitment to sustainability.

Today, I want to highlight seven key aspects of our performance. First, our capital expenditures and operating expenses demonstrated disciplined execution in a fast-changing clean energy environment. Second, our operating capacity and generation output reached new highs, reflecting reliable dispatchable energy delivery. Third, we secured significant new power purchase agreements with attractive average pricing. Fourth, our overall performance included standout achievements like record deployments and revenue growth. Fifth, PPA pricing trends showed resilience alongside successful contract extensions. Sixth, our strategic priorities position us strongly for the coming quarters and year ahead. And seventh, our debt levels and financing costs remained optimized for growth.

Now, I'll hand over the call to Sarah Kline to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Mark. Our financial performance in the Q3 was outstanding. Revenue reached $1.45 billion, representing a 28% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 28.5%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $312 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $250 million, or $1.05 per share. We ended the quarter with $450 million in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Diving deeper into our capital expenditures and operating expenses, which underscore our approach amid the evolving clean energy landscape. Solara Renewables is a vertically integrated leader in utility-scale solar PV, onshore wind, and long-duration energy storage, with over 15 GW of operational assets across North America, Europe, and select APAC markets. Our results benefit from tailwinds like the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act, the EU's REPowerEU plan, and global grid constraints boosting demand for dispatchable renewables.

On CAPEX, we deployed $1.45 billion in the quarter, up 18% year-over-year and aligning with our full-year guidance of $5.2-5.6 billion. This acceleration helps secure low-cost engineering, procurement, and construction contracts and IRA Investment Tax Credits before any potential post-2025 policy changes. The breakdown includes solar PV at 62% or $897 million, mainly for our 1.2 GW SunForge bifacial TOPCon module projects in the U.S. Southwest and Texas ERCOT grid. We achieved a 12% sequential cost reduction per MWdc to $0.82/W, due to locked-in polysilicon supply from LONGi Green Energy at pre-inflation rates and our proprietary n-type cell passivation technology, which improves levelized cost of energy by 8-10% over PERC baselines. Notably, $250 million went to tracker systems from Nextracker to address wind load risks in high-velocity areas.

Onshore wind accounted for 24% or $348 million, focused on our 600 MW AeroBlade portfolio in the U.S. Midwest and Poland, using 5.X MW Siemens Gamesa turbines with 150m rotors for capacity factors over 45%. CAPEX per MW was $1.35 million, down 5% year-over-year thanks to U.S. domestic content bonuses under IRA Section 45X—we reached 55% U.S.-sourced steel and towers, qualifying for $40/kW credits. European challenges included a 15% steel price increase from Ukraine-related disruptions, but we hedged 70% with forward contracts.

Battery storage and grid tech took 14% or $203 million, up 35% year-over-year, funding 450 MWh of BESS paired with solar/wind hybrids. Key spending was for LFP cells from CATL at $85/kWh landed cost, integrated with Fluence Energy's Gridstack for 4-hour duration. We're advancing virtual power plants with AI-orchestrated black-start capabilities, capturing California's LCFS credits and ERCOT ancillary services revenue, which added $15 million in Q3 merchant uplift.

Our CAPEX efficiency shows through project internal rates of return floored at 12-14%, with EPC timelines at 14 months versus industry 18-month averages. We're front-loading 2025 spending into late 2024 to benefit from module prices down 22% year-over-year per IRENA data and U.S. manufacturing growth—our Arizona thin-film fab, inspired by First Solar's CdTe tech, adds 2 GW by Q1 2025 at $0.25/W intensity. We build in a 10% buffer for copper at $4.50/lb, supported by our $2.1 billion undrawn credit facility and 3.2x net debt/EBITDA.

For OPEX, $312 million was flat year-over-year, enabling 12% gross margin expansion to 28.5%. Adjusted for one-offs like $18 million in Texas freeze repairs, core OPEX per MW was $14.5k, beating our $16k target.

Operations and maintenance was 48% or $150 million: solar availability at 99.2%, wind at 98.5%, aided by our Predix AI platform—similar to GE Vernova's—reducing unplanned downtime 22% with drone thermography and vibration analytics. BESS OPEX dropped to $8/kWh annualized via thermal runaway firmware. U.S. assets gained from IRA PTC adders, while EU costs rose 8% on labor under Germany's EEG surcharges.

SG&A at 28% or $87 million, 5.2% of revenue down from 6.1% year-over-year, from insourcing PPA origination—800 MW corporate offtakes with Meta and Google at $35-42/MWh—and automating permitting, cutting U.S. queues from 24 to 16 months.

R&D and other at 24% or $75 million: $42 million for perovskite-silicon tandems targeting 35% efficiency with Oxford PV, and hydrogen electrolyzers for our 100 MW green H2 pilot in Iberia, aligning with EU IPCEI funding for Power-to-X by 2027.

By region, U.S. OPEX 15% below plan on IRA labor credits; Europe up 7% on REPowerEU biodiversity costs; APAC light at $5k/MW via Vietnam solar under FiT 4.0.

Overall, this drove EBITDA of $456 million, up 24% year-over-year, with $320 million cash generation funding 65% of CAPEX internally. For FY2024, CAPEX at the top of range, OPEX $1.25-1.30 billion, with 2-3% efficiencies from VPP scaling and localization.

Turning to debt levels and financing costs, our total gross debt is $5.2 billion, including $3.1 billion non-recourse project financing, $1.8 billion corporate revolver and term loans, and $0.3 billion construction financing. Net debt is $4.75 billion after $450 million cash. Leverage improved to 4.2x net debt-to-EBITDA from 4.5x year-end. Interest coverage at 3.8x.

Blended cost of debt at 4.15%, down 25 bps year-over-year via refinancing: $800 million on Texas wind portfolio to green bonds at 3.85%, rated BBB+, with ESG demand from BlackRock and CalPERS. Tax equity closed $420 million for BESS, reducing WACC by 150 bps. 75% variable exposure swapped at SOFR + 175 bps.

U.S. debt at low costs tied to IRA projects; Europe EIB loans at 2.9%; APAC higher at 5.2%, mitigated by ADB syndication. For $6-7 billion pipeline needs, 50/50 project/corporate split, with $1.5 billion backstops. Costs to stabilize at 4.0-4.2% in 2025.

I'll now turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our project development activities.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Sarah. Our project development pipeline continues to expand, with 15 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, further contributing to our revenue and profitability. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to accelerate our growth.

In Q3, we secured 1.2 GW of new PPAs across five utility-scale projects, lifting total contracted backlog to 4.8 GW, up 35% year-over-year. This includes 850 MWac solar-plus-storage hybrids with 350 MWh BESS and 350 MW standalone wind. Average tenor 18 years with 2% CPI escalators.

Counterparties: 60% investment-grade utilities like Southern California Edison and NextEra, 30% hyperscalers like 200 MW shaped PPA with Microsoft for Azure, 10% C&I like Walmart. Average price $38/MWh levelized, up 12% from Q3 2023, flat sequentially. Solar+storage at $42/MWh with ERCOT arbitrage; standalone solar $36/MWh with 32% DC:AC; wind $35/MWh.

U.S. Southwest 700 MW at $45/MWh on NEM 3.0; ERCOT 300 MW at $32/MWh with merchant tails; Europe 100 MW German wind at €48/MWh. Prices rebounded 18% per LevelTen, with AI yield forecasting for 5-7% uplift. Hub-and-spoke model fast-tracks 2 GW. Q4: 1.5-2 GW at $39-41/MWh.

On trends and extensions, new PPA prices softened to $24-28/MWh globally from hardware deflation, but U.S. bifurcated: Southwest $22-26/MWh hybrids, PJM $32-36/MWh. Europe €18-22/MWh solar, UK €25/MWh offshore. APAC India INR 2.0-2.2/kWh. Blended $29/MWh, 95% contracted.

Extensions on 1.8 GW at $32/MWh average, up 12%: California solar with Google post-microinverter/storage; Midwest wind with AWS. Corporate PPAs now 40%. U.S. Southwest 55% volume. Q4 extensions 2.5 GW at $25-30/MWh. PPA 2.0 clauses for dynamic pricing.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Jordan. We are dedicated to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing advanced technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies like bifacial TOPCon and perovskite tandems, energy storage solutions including LFP and flow batteries, and smart grid technologies with AI optimization and VPPs. Our SolaraOS platform manages assets with predictive maintenance, drone analytics, and ML forecasting for precise output. These advancements, including Enphase microinverters, Vestas upgrades, and Fluence integrations, boost yields, cut downtime, and enable value stacking in ancillary markets. We believe that these technologies will play a pivotal role in transforming the energy landscape.

Next, Marcus Green will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Marcus Green:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. Sustainability is a core value at Solara Renewables, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon footprint, improving energy efficiency across our fleet, and promoting responsible resource management in supply chains. Our agrivoltaics combine solar with agriculture, generating dual revenue while preserving biodiversity. Community engagement includes local hiring, H2 pilots for green fuels, and Scope 3 reductions via electrified logistics. We're advancing net-zero through IRA/REPowerEU alignment, with biodiversity offsets and REC bundling.

Now, Taylor Brooks will provide operational highlights.

Taylor Brooks:
Thank you, Marcus. Our operational performance remains strong. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets. We are implementing best practices in areas such as asset management, maintenance, and supply chain management. We are also investing in training and development to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to succeed.

Specifically, at quarter-end, total operating capacity was 5,247 MW, up 26% year-over-year from 4,162 MW, with 850 MW commissioned including 400 MW SunForge solar and 250 MW wind repowers, net of minor decommissioning. Generation reached 4,856 GWh, up 19% year-over-year, with 41.2% capacity factor, 210 bps better, outperforming EIA solar 24.8% and wind 35.4%.

Mix: 52% solar PV 2,729 MW generating 1,892 GWh up 32% at 27.6% factor with Enphase IQ8; 38% wind 1,994 MW at 2,312 GWh, onshore 38.4%, offshore 44.7%; 7% BESS 367 MW/1,120 MWh discharging 482 GWh equiv.; 3% green H2 157 MW equiv.

North America 3,421 MW 65%, 3,214 GWh up 28% with IRA $320M YTD; EMEA 1,512 MW 1,412 GWh; APAC 314 MW 230 GWh up 45%.

Initiatives: repowering 430 MW YTD for 15-20% uplift; digital twins with Siemens for ±2% accuracy, $12M ancillaries; hybrid+storage 70% pipeline. FY24 guide: 6,200 MW +18%, 20,500 GWh +22%.

I'll turn it back to Mark Thompson for closing remarks.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you, Taylor. To summarize, Solara Renewables had an exceptional Q3. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our focus on sustainability will drive continued growth and success.

Looking ahead, our priorities center on capacity expansion, tech leadership, and diversification. FY24 revenue $2.1B up 28%, EBITDA $485M at 23.1%, solar EPC backlog $4.8B up 35%. Q1 2025 capex $350M for 8 GW module factory expansion and 3 GWh battery line, U.S. revenue +45% to $1.5B. R&D $180M for 32.5% tandems, SolaraFlow storage, 20 MW H2 at $2.50/kg. Europe/APAC/LatAm growth with floating PV, SECI wins. Q1 revenue $580-620M, FY25 $2.8-3.0B +33-43%, EBITDA $650-700M. FCF $200M positive.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Instructions. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Mark Thompson:
Thanks, John. International expansion is key to our diversification. Europe doubled revenues to $450 million in 2024 via REPowerEU, with Q1 2025 800 MW in Spain/Italy at €22/MWh and floating PV. APAC up 50% with 1.1 GW India SECI compliant modules, Gujarat localization. LatAm like 300 MW Atacama with AES for H2. Regional mix FY25: U.S. 65%, EMEA 20%, APAC 12%, LatAm 3%, 80% USD hedged.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
How are you addressing the challenge of intermittency associated with renewable energy sources?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Lisa. Intermittency is core to our innovation. 70% pipeline includes 4-hour BESS for firming, with 92% utilization in CAISO/ERCOT capturing $45/MWh spreads. SolaraFlow flow batteries offer 20-hour duration at 85% efficiency. Hybrids, VPPs, AI forecasting mitigate duck curves. Green H2 pilots hedge long-term, with 1.2 GWh contracts and repowers boosting factors 15-20%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
Can you discuss the impact of government subsidies and tax incentives on your profitability?

Sarah Kline:
Absolutely, Mike. Subsidies like IRA ITC/PTC are transformative—we monetized $1.2B YTD, $320M Q2 alone, enabling 210 bps margin expansion. Domestic content 45X $40/kW, transferability cuts WACC 150 bps, IRR 7.5-8%. REPowerEU subsidies for Europe, DOE grants $150M H2. These fortify 65-70% EBITDA margins, de-risking vs. merchant, with FY24 $2.5B target.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Patel:
What are your expectations for electricity demand growth in the coming years?

Mark Thompson:
Emily, demand growth is robust, driven by data centers, EVs, electrification. Hyperscalers like Microsoft/Google RFPs at 10-15 GW annually, AI baseload needs shaped PPAs. U.S. heat domes, Texas HB8 boost ERCOT. Globally, India's 500 GW, EU net-zero. We see 20% CAGR pipeline matching 5-7% annual demand rise per EIA/IEA, with our 45 GW development 3+ years visibility.

Operator:
Instructions. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Mark Thompson for any closing remarks.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Solara Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
